title: Weekly pilot: efficiency tuning rhythm call

Agreed to run an A/B with revised batch window and raise burst capacity for peak hour, Redwood to share tuned config and updated SLO runbook.

continuous batching window and max concurrency targets
KV cache hit behavior for repeated prompts
fallbacks: model variants vs region routing

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-24
- Start: 10:30 AM PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Head of ML, MapleGrid), Riya Kapoor (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete): Weekly poke on pilot throughput, continuous batching tuning, queueing and KV cache observations. Agreement to run spike A/B and share config + histograms.

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, we got about 40 minutes, we'll go quick. Um Diego and I will lead, Evan you mentioned an interesting blip overnight?
[00:28] Evan Park: yeah, cool thanks. so between 2am and 3am PT we saw a couple of tail events, p95 jumped from 190ms to 620ms for about 10 minutes, cost didn't skyrocket but it's enough to worry the SREs, they flagged queue growth.
[01:03] Diego Morales: okay, can you clarify — was that on the hosted model or your dedicated pool?
[01:17] Riya Kapoor: this was on the dedicated pilot pool, the one you provisioned via the trial reserved capacity, same topology as earlier, 4 x A100-ish nodes.
[01:36] Diego Morales: got it. quick sidebar, our telemetry shows an increase in small, sequential requests that defeat batching sometimes — there may be a pattern of microbursts that arrive inside the prefix window and then a lull, so continuous batching configured at X ms might be coalescing less.
[02:05] Samir Patel: when you say "coalescing less" do you mean you're dropping requests or delaying them? our concern is user-facing latency, not internal batching tradeoffs.
[02:22] Laura Chen: great question. Diego?
[02:28] Diego Morales: so it's delaying a little — requests are queued while the batch window tries to fill, if concurrency hits max_concurrency we start to throttle and you see queue growth and tail p95 inflation. In your case the microburst pattern + a couple of long-running requests filled async slots and prevented expected batching efficiency.
[02:57] Evan Park: hmm, yeah one of our services had a retry storm at 02:10 which probably amplified. client retries are fairly aggressive right now. Riya can pull that?
[03:12] Riya Kapoor: yep we'll attach the trace.
[03:18] Diego Morales: okay from Redwood side we think two levers: (1) tighten batch_window to reduce per-request wait but maybe lower batch sizes, and (2) bump max_concurrency slightly to reduce throttling under microbursts. there's also continuous KV cache warmup issues — we saw only ~28% KV hit rate for repeated prompts vs expected 45%.
[03:46] Evan Park: KV hits that low will cost us a lot. are you saying it's an onboarding / tokenization mismatch?
[03:54] Diego Morales: could be tokenization or prompt framing differences. sometimes small whitespace or punctuation differences make cache keys mismatch — also our prefix cache expiration is set conservatively.
[04:12] Laura Chen: quick check — are you using client side dedupe or any normalized prompt preproc?
[04:21] Riya Kapoor: we do a light normalization but not strict canonicalization, we can try to tighten that.
[04:27] Diego Morales: great, that will help. also sending you a short README for KV cache best practices, will include lookups and canonicalization tips.
[04:40] Evan Park: perfect, thanks. on the concurrency number — what do you recommend for our RPS profile? we peaked at about 420 RPS during the earlier stress run.
[04:54] Diego Morales: with 4 nodes and your current model variant, we recommend starting max_concurrency at 160 per node then tune to observed latencies. so overall pool concurrency ~640, but you may want lower to keep p95 < 250ms. Right now your current config is 480 which is why you're hitting backpressure.
[05:17] Samir Patel: is that per-GPU or per-node? we run mixed vGPU config.
[05:25] Diego Morales: per-node, apologies. per-GPU would be smaller; we can map to your topology in the config. I'll export a mapping table.
[05:36] Laura Chen: Diego, can you pull the histogram you mentioned? Evan, you'll want to see batches/sec and tokens/batch.
[05:46] Diego Morales: yes, I pulled the last 48h histograms before the call — sending after. Quick note, we saw two modes: steady small batches ~8-12 tokens/batch most of the time and occasional 70-120 token batches during larger multi-turn flows. The variance makes static batch windows suboptimal.
[06:09] Evan Park: so continuous batching adaptive windowing could help? I thought Redwood had an adaptive algorithm?
[06:18] Diego Morales: we do have an adaptive mode but it's conservative by default to avoid latency regressions. For pilots we can safely nudge parameters: reduce min_batch_wait and increase max aggregation for burst alignment. That usually yields a ~12-18% tokens/sec improvement at the same p95.
[06:40] Riya Kapoor: what's the risk of decreasing min_batch_wait?
[06:45] Diego Morales: you may see slightly smaller average batch sizes leading to marginally higher cost per token but better tail latency, it's a tradeoff. We can do A/B to quantify.
[06:58] Laura Chen: side security check — Samir you had asked about audit logs and KMS for private keys?
[07:06] Samir Patel: yes, our compliance team wants confirmation that all request logs are masked and can be exported to our SIEM, and keys are customer-managed.
[07:19] Laura Chen: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and audit log exports. For the hosted pilot, logs are redacted by default and we can push an export job. We'll attach SOC2 and KMS docs to the notes.
[07:36] Samir Patel: great, please send.
[07:42] Evan Park: going back to the 2am event — any suggestion for reducing blast radius during client retry storms?
[07:51] Diego Morales: yes, two improvements: (1) server-side adaptive backpressure that returns a 429 with Retry-After when queues exceed a threshold, and (2) require your clients to implement exponential backoff with jitter. We can also enable per-token budget shaping to keep a soft cap on tokens/sec.
[08:14] Riya Kapoor: we can tweak clients but need to coordinate release. For the short term can you enable server-side 429 behaviour for the pool?
[08:23] Diego Morales: yes we can flip that flag for the pilot. We'll also enable more aggressive queue trimming for the spike window.
[08:32] Laura Chen: note: enabling 429s will change error profiles for product teams—Riya please share a brief comms note.
[08:42] Riya Kapoor: will do.
[08:45] Evan Park: Diego you mentioned KV hit rate — do you think a change in prefix expiration would help?
[08:53] Diego Morales: absolutely, increase prefix_ttl from 30s to 120s for your steady customers helps warm the cache; downside is memory usage on the node increases. For the duration of the pilot spike it's worth trying.
[09:07] Samir Patel: memory is okay for now. do you have numbers on memory vs hit-rate tradeoffs?
[09:14] Diego Morales: yes — sending an appendix. Roughly doubling TTL moved hit rate from 28% to 44% in a similar workload in our benchmarks.
[09:26] Laura Chen: okay action registered: Diego will export histograms and memory/tradeoff appendix.
[09:33] Evan Park: quick thought — could region routing help during this window? route some traffic to another region to spread load?
[09:42] Diego Morales: yes you can route by policy; we also support automated fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency rises above SLO. But for enterprise you prefer to stay on the same model for consistency right?
[09:54] Samir Patel: yes prefer same model but fallback might be acceptable for non-critical endpoints.
[10:00] Laura Chen: agreed. we'll document policy.
[10:06] Diego Morales: a proposed immediate change set for the A/B spike:
- Reduce batch_window_ms from 25 -> 12 (Variant A)
- Keep current 25ms as Variant B
- Increase max_concurrency per node 20% for spike window
- Increase prefix_ttl to 120s during spike
- Enable server-side 429 when queue depth > threshold

[10:38] Evan Park: sounds good. what's the expected token/sec change?
[10:42] Diego Morales: we expect tokens/sec up by ~10-20% on the adaptive variant; p95 should drop 10-30ms in the steady case but in bursts you should see fewer large tails. Cost delta expected <5% for the spike.
[10:58] Riya Kapoor: please put the exact numbers in the config doc so SREs can review.
[11:05] Laura Chen: we'll put a small table. Diego, can you put recommended max_concurrency per GPU for their mixed vGPU?
[11:13] Diego Morales: yes mapping included.
[11:16] Evan Park: any concerns about the KV cache canonicalization change? we'll need to coordinate changes on our side to normalize prompts.
[11:25] Diego Morales: low risk — we'll provide a small Python snippet to canonicalize common patterns.
[11:30] Riya Kapoor: great. also, for the A/B we'll need Redwood to stand up a separate pilot route so we can split traffic 50/50.
[11:40] Diego Morales: can do, Redwood will create a split route and label variants. We'll also add sampling telemetry to trace per-variant p95.
[11:50] Samir Patel: timeline?
[11:53] Laura Chen: propose Wed 09/29 spike, configure tomorrow EOD, Diego sends artifacts, Riya provides traffic trace by EOD Monday.
[12:05] Evan Park: sounds good. last Q from my side: any thought on model quantization or smaller footprint model for fallbacks?
[12:15] Diego Morales: we can use a quantized variant for fallback — latency improves, quality slightly impacted. We'll flag recommended model variants and typical quality delta in the appendix.
[12:30] Riya Kapoor: please include comparison table.
[12:34] Laura Chen: ok wrapping up, quick recap of next steps and action owners (we'll also drop these in the CRM and share the deck):
[12:42] Laura Chen: Diego exports histograms and mapping table (due 09/26). Laura shares revised pilot config + runbook (due 09/25). Riya provides traffic traces and client retry policy (due 09/28). Redwood to enable temporary burst capacity and 429 behaviour for the spike on Wed.
[13:00] Evan Park: thanks all, looking forward to the A/B results.
[13:05] Samir Patel: thanks.
[13:08] Laura Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links: pilot-config.xlsx, batch-histograms.csv, kv-cache-appendix.pdf (links will be in the follow-up email). Bye.

Post-meeting notes: shared artifacts: https://redwood-internal.example/pilot/MapleGrid/pilot-config.xlsx (redacted link), https://redwood-internal.example/pilot/MapleGrid/batch-histograms.csv.

Quality notes: automated transcript contains mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache in places). Manual noise: occasional crosstalk and overlapping speech at ~08:40-08:50 mark.
